inspection_summary: Inspected all 573 normalized lines. The source develops the same RH closure criterion through four linked Hilbert-space representations: analytic Hardy functions, fractional-part functions in L2((0,1]), a piecewise-constant subspace, and weighted sequences. Its reusable mechanisms are Mobius partial sums as approximate inverses, Hadamard-factorization bounds supplying norm convergence, common-zero evaluation as the reverse obstruction, and semigroup invariance upgrading containment of one cyclic vector to totality. The final distance/Gram-determinant proposal is retained together with the author's warning that the available formulas are poorly suited to estimation. Prose is generally coherent, but several displayed formulas have damaged extraction and are explicitly isolated or marked for scan verification rather than reconstructed.

accepted_units.title: RH as closure and totality of periodic sequences
accepted_units.why_material: This is the source's most discrete criterion: a constant vector lies in the closed span of simple fractional-part sequences exactly when those sequences are total, and both conditions are equivalent to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the weighted inner product, the vectors gamma_l and gamma, the definition of totality, and the entire theorem statement so the criterion is coherent without outside reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The norm, inner product, and gamma_l displays are formula-dependent and visibly split across lines 31-40; verify those displays against the retained scan before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Harmonic approximation meaning and robustness to equivalent weights
accepted_units.why_material: The text interprets totality as approximation of arbitrary mildly growing sequences by simple periodic ones and shows that the criterion is invariant under any quadratically comparable weight through an invertible identity map.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the distinction between the survey's theorem and the cited paper, then supplies both the approximation interpretation and the norm-equivalence argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low apart from a stray extraction artifact on line 70; the substantive claims are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free RH formulation inside a Hardy space
accepted_units.why_material: It reframes RH as analyticity of reciprocal zeta on the right half of the critical strip and places the later closure argument in a functional Hilbert space whose norm is controlled by critical-line boundary values.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the zeta symmetry argument, the definition of the half-plane Omega, the Hardy-space norm, and the boundary-value identification needed later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The set display for Omega and the norm/boundary-value displays at lines 96-120 are extraction-damaged; their prose-level roles are recoverable, but exact formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Parameterized zeta functions encode the Hardy-space closure criterion
accepted_units.why_material: The family F_lambda and discrete subfamily G_l package a zeta factor with a pole-cancelling coefficient, yielding equivalent continuous-parameter and discrete closed-span formulations of RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes membership motivation, the target vector E, the complete theorem statement, and the stated implication order.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: exact powers and normalizations in F_lambda, G_l, and E should be checked against the scan before symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: Uniform Mobius Dirichlet bounds under RH
accepted_units.why_material: The proof requires more than pointwise reciprocal-zeta convergence: a quantitative Littlewood lemma supplies uniform control of finite Mobius sums on shifted half-planes, enabling later dominated convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the reciprocal Dirichlet series, the distinction between the unnecessary arithmetic description of Mobius and the needed analytic statement, and the lemma's relation to Littlewood's theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The summation display in lines 197-199 is compacted by extraction; the qualitative uniformity and parameter dependence are explicit in prose, while the exact bound is formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Two-stage construction of an approximate inverse
accepted_units.why_material: Mobius-weighted finite combinations first converge in Hardy norm to shifted reciprocal-zeta approximants H_epsilon, after which the shift tends to zero toward E; this exposes the constructive core of the closure implication.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the definitions of H_{L,epsilon} and H_epsilon, both convergence stages, and the precise remaining domination obligation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence in lines 206-242; coefficient powers, the H_epsilon display, and limit directions require scan verification even though the two-stage mechanism is clear from prose.

accepted_units.title: Zero geometry yields the domination needed for norm convergence
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH, pairing zeros in the Hadamard product gives monotonic control of the completed zeta function under a real shift; gamma asymptotics then yield an integrable bound for H_epsilon and complete the constructive implication.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the factorization, the shift inequality (also noted as an RH reformulation), the gamma-ratio estimate, and the final square-integrable majorant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent throughout; several products, ratios, and exponents are visually fragile in extraction, so exact inequalities and constants must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: A zero in Omega forces the entire generating family into a proper kernel
accepted_units.why_material: The reverse implication is a concise functional-analytic obstruction: any off-line zeta zero annihilates every F_lambda, so their closed span lies in a proper evaluation kernel and cannot contain the nonvanishing target E.
accepted_units.context_note: The inclusion of the continuity of point evaluation is essential to closedness of the obstructing subspace.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; only the final E(rho)=1/rho display is formula-dependent and is legible.

accepted_units.title: The discrete generating family can be thinned to square-free indices
accepted_units.why_material: Because Mobius coefficients vanish off square-free integers, the same construction proves the closure criterion using a strictly thinner family, separating the essential support of the approximants from the full indexing set.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a direct source-local consequence of the previously defined approximants.

accepted_units.title: Fractional-part functions give the original L2 closure and totality criterion
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem realizes RH as approximation of the constant function and, equivalently, totality of a parameterized family of fractional-part functions in L2((0,1]).
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the ambient Hilbert space, definitions of f_lambda and the constant target, and all three equivalent statements.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining fractional-part formula at lines 313-317 is extraction-sensitive; verify its exact bracketing and coefficients against the scan.

accepted_units.title: An isometric Mellin transform transports the L2 problem to Hardy space
accepted_units.why_material: The transform supplies the structural bridge between interval functions and analytic functions, with indicator functions furnishing a total family that establishes isometry on the whole source space.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains analyticity, the norm-preservation argument on interval indicators, and their totality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed transform and auxiliary integral are damaged: line 329 appears to show an inconsistent upper limit and lines 336-341 are fragmented. Do not reconstruct them from memory; scan verification is required for exact formulas.

accepted_units.title: Fractional-part generators map to the analytic zeta family
accepted_units.why_material: The calculation identifies the Mellin image of each f_lambda with minus F_lambda, making the two closure problems genuinely equivalent rather than merely analogous.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the initial half-plane calculation, telescoping series, subtraction step, and analytic continuation to Omega.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: integral limits, fractional-part brackets, powers, and the telescoping identity are formula-dependent and partially garbled in lines 351-398; exact reuse requires comparison with the scan.

accepted_units.title: Semigroup invariance promotes one-vector containment to totality
accepted_units.why_material: After transporting the closure statement, multiplication by inner functions preserves the span and generates transforms of a total indicator family from E, converting approximation of one target into totality of all fractional-part generators.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts with the isometric transfer of RH to L2 and retains the full invariant-subspace argument for the implication from closure to totality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive normalizations in Theta_mu, M_mu(F_lambda), and the indicator transform should be scan-checked; the invariant-subspace logic is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: The closure proof is an approximate-inverse problem for zeta
accepted_units.why_material: The author identifies the conceptual heart as constructing approximate inverses to zeta in a weighted Hardy space and contrasts the natural Mobius partial sums with the less motivated original complex-analytic route, while acknowledging where difficult estimates remain hidden.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves both the simplifying interpretation and its limitation: the conditional estimate and Littlewood lemma still contain omitted Phragmen-Lindelof-type work.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; the weight |E(s)|^2 is the only formula-level dependency.

accepted_units.title: A step-function subspace turns reciprocal parameters into discrete generators
accepted_units.why_material: The closed subspace of functions constant on reciprocal intervals supports generators g_l=f_{1/l}; their intervalwise values make the later unitary identification with periodic sequences possible.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the subspace definition, the discrete family, its membership in the subspace, and the statement that this is the Baez-Duarte refinement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The interval endpoints and equation (5) are visibly garbled in lines 451-474. The prose supports the discretization and membership claim, but exact pointwise values must be verified against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Discrete dilations upgrade the Baez-Duarte closure criterion to totality
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 7 combines the reciprocal-indexed closure criterion with a semigroup of isometries whose orbit of the constant function contains a total family of interval indicators, proving the discrete family is total exactly under RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the equivalence statement, Mellin transfer for the constructive direction, the dilation-semigroup invariant-span argument, and the reverse transfer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The piecewise definition of T_m and the identity for T_m(g_l) at lines 500-514 are extraction-defective. Their exact scaling and indices require scan verification; only the surrounding stated isometry, semigroup, and invariance consequences are safely recoverable from text.

accepted_units.title: Sampling on reciprocal integers unitarily transfers totality to weighted sequences
accepted_units.why_material: A unitary sampling map sends the constant step function to gamma and each discrete generator to gamma_l, making the opening sequence theorem a direct reformulation and carrying over square-free thinning.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition and both named images of the unitary map plus the square-free refinement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The sampling display is formula-dependent but readable; equation (5), on which the image of g_l depends, remains scan-dependent as flagged in u15.

accepted_units.title: Finite-dimensional distance decay is equivalent to RH but Gram formulas resist estimation
accepted_units.why_material: The source converts density into decay of distances to initial finite spans, proposes a strong asymptotic, and explains that the resulting ratio of Gram determinants is explicit yet poorly suited to calculation or estimation, recording both a possible route and its bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the definition of D(L), its RH equivalence, the conjectural squared-distance scale, the determinant representation, and the author's negative assessment.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants in the conjectured asymptotic and the finite-sum formulas alluded to are formula-dependent; the inner-product sums themselves are not displayed, so no reconstruction is attempted.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One criterion across four Hilbert representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Isometric or unitary maps preserve the same closure/totality question while progressively changing analytic functions into fractional-part functions, step functions, and weighted sequences.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact formulas for both transforms and the step-function sampling identity are scan-dependent; this synthesis establishes source-stated equivalence, not a new proof beyond those bridges.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Semigroup invariance as a cyclic-to-total promotion principle
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: In both continuous and discrete representations, an invariant closed span that contains one target vector must contain the orbit-generated indicator family, and that known-total family forces totality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source proves this only for its particular multiplication and dilation semigroups; no general cyclicity theorem is asserted.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Mobius approximate inverses with support thinning
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The constructive direction treats partial sums of reciprocal zeta's Mobius series as approximate inverses, uses zero geometry for norm domination, and automatically restricts the necessary generators to square-free indices.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The argument is conditional on RH and on substantial analytic estimates whose proofs are omitted; approximation here is Hilbert-space closure, not pointwise inversion everywhere.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Constructive closure versus common-zero obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The equivalence has asymmetric mechanisms: RH constructs norm-convergent approximants, whereas failure of RH supplies a single continuous evaluation functional that separates the target from the whole generating span.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This contrast is specific to the stated functional Hilbert space and does not measure approximation rates.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From qualitative density to a finite-dimensional distance observable
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The unitary sequence criterion makes RH equivalent to vanishing distance from gamma to growing finite spans, suggesting Gram determinants as finite observables of the density problem.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper explicitly says the resulting determinant formulas are unsuitable for effective estimation and presents no successful bound.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after all 573 lines: every source-local definition, equivalence, representation bridge, approximation mechanism, obstruction, thinning result, method comparison, and proposed quantitative route is represented. Further segmentation would isolate routine algebra, repeat theorem implications already covered, rely on damaged displays without scan verification, or select page furniture and references.
stop_reason: The source ends after a fully inspected distance/Gram-determinant discussion and bibliography. All usable mathematical mechanisms are assigned to accepted units; omitted passages are page furniture, routine derivational detail, repetitions, or explicitly marked extraction-defective formulas, not material excluded by a quota.
